identity.title: ALMA Observations of Two Massive and Dense MALT90 Clumps

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report Atacama Large Millimeter Array observations of 3 mm dust continuum emission and line emission, in HCO$^{+}$, H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$, N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ and CH$_{3}$CN, towards two massive and dense clumps

distance_source.value: reference (2) in Table 1, not identified in the text

question.value: How do massive and dense clumps in prestellar and protostellar phases fragment into cores, and what are the cores' physical and kinematic properties?

evidence.quote: made with the goal of investigating their fragmentation characteristics at angular scales of $\sim$1$\ensuremath{''}$.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00645.S.
We made ALMA Band 3 (86-116 GHz) dust continuum and molecular line observations towards the MDCs AGAL333 and AGAL329.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two setups: N2H+, CH3CN and 3 continuum SPWs; HCO+, H13CO+ and 2 continuum SPWs. Line SPWs 117.19 MHz wide; continuum SPWs 1875 MHz wide

evidence.quote: In the first one, five separate spectral windows (SPW) were used, three for continuum observations and two for observations of the N$_{2}$H$^{+}$J=1$\rightarrow$0 and CH$_{3}$CN J=5$\rightarrow$4 lines.

arrays.value: 12 m array and 7 m ACA, single pointing

evidence.quote: single pointing observations were carried out, as part of Cycle 4, during Dec 2016 and Jan 2017 using both the 12 m array and 7m Atacama Compact Array (ACA).

angular_resolution.value: 1.46"x1.34" (PA 155°) for AGAL329; 1.46"x1.33" (PA 138°) for AGAL333 in continuum

evidence.quote: The angular resolution achieved in the continuum observations are 1.46$\ensuremath{''}\times1.34\ensuremath{''}$ (P.A. 155$\ensuremath{^\circ}$)

evidence.quote: The integration time on source in each of the setups was 23 and 32 minutes for the 7m and 12m array observations, respectively.
during Dec 2016 and Jan 2017

analysis_steps.goal: Identify cores in the 3 mm continuum

method.value: Astrodendro and Clumpfind; Clumpfind parameters adopted

evidence.quote: Given the similarities, in the remaining of this paper we will use the parameters of the cores determined from the Clumpfind method

key_parameters.value: Astrodendro: Fmin=3 sigma, delta=1 sigma, Amin=1 beam

evidence.quote: we adopted F$_{min}$=3$\sigma$, $\delta$=1$\sigma$ and A$_{min}$ = 1 beam.

key_parameters.value: Clumpfind: Tlow=3 sigma, dT=2 sigma, Smin=1 beam

evidence.quote: we adopted T$_{low}$=3$\sigma$, $\Delta$T=2$\sigma$ and S$_{min}$ = 1 beam.

validation.value: Compared the two algorithms; fluxes and sizes similar

evidence.quote: We find that the flux densities and angular sizes of the structures (cores) obtained from both methods are similar.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit core line spectra for velocity, width and optical depth

method.value: Hyperfine fit of N2H+ with pyspeckit; Gaussian fit to H13CO+; Gaussian or two components for complex cores

evidence.quote: The red line shows the result of a simultaneous fit to the emission from the whole hyperfine structure for a single velocity component, made using the task *pyspeckit.models* in *PySpecKit*
From a least squares fit to the data we derived the rotational temperatures given in column 8 of Table [\[tab:Trot\]]

validation.value: N2H+ and H13CO+ velocities and widths agree

evidence.quote: the velocities and line widths of the cores derived from both lines are in good agreement

analysis_steps.goal: Derive CH3CN rotational temperatures and column densities

method.value: Rotational diagram, least-squares fit to K=0-4 lines of J=5-4

evidence.quote: We use the standard rotational diagram analysis ( (cite: Turner1991; Sutton1995)) which assumes that the lines are optically thin and that the population levels are characterized by a single excitation temperature (LTE assumption).

key_parameters.value: Cores with at least three K lines above 3 sigma

evidence.quote: for which at least three lines in the 5$_K$ - 4$_K$ K-ladder were detected above the 3$\sigma$ level

assumptions.value: LTE, optically thin; Q(T) from Araya2005

validation.value: Optical-depth-corrected diagram gives differences within errors

evidence.quote: the differences in the derived temperatures and column densities are well within the errors determined from the “traditional" approach

analysis_steps.goal: Compute core masses, column densities, virial parameters

method.value: Optically thin dust mass from 3 mm flux with Trot (clump T otherwise); alpha_vir=Mvir/M with Mvir=5 sigma^2 R/G

evidence.quote: For cores in which no rotational temperature is available we adopted the temperature of the clump.

key_parameters.value: Core radius from geometric mean of Clumpfind semi-axes

evidence.quote: The radius of the cores were computed from the geometric mean of the semi-major and minor axis determined from Clumpfind

assumptions.value: Rgd=100; k100GHz=0.21 cm2/g; mu_H2=2.8; virial equilibrium for 0.71<alpha<1.4

evidence.quote: The uncertainties in the mass are estimated to be $\sim$40%

method.value: Maximum likelihood power-law fit to the eCDF of the combined core sample (AGAL329, AGAL333, AGAL305)

evidence.quote: the value of the $\alpha$ index that best reproduces the eCDF, using the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) method, is $-1.33\pm$0.15

key_parameters.value: Mass limits 0.9, 0.7, 1.4 Msun (3 sigma flux at clump temperature)

evidence.quote: The mass sensitivity limits are 0.9, 0.7 and 1.4 M$_{\odot}$ for AGAL329, AGAL333 and AGAL305, respectively.

fitting.value: MLE of a power law dN/dM ∝ M^alpha

evidence.quote: Assuming that the core mass function (CMF) can be described by a power-law $dN/dM$ $\propto$ $M^{\alpha}$, the value of the $\alpha$ index that best reproduces the eCDF, using the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) method
the 90% confidence interval is $-1.58$ to $-1.08$

analysis_steps.goal: Infall model fit for the central AGAL329 core

method.value: Fit HCO+ spectrum with Hill5 infall model of De Vries & Myers; mass infall rate from 4 pi R^2 n mu mH v_in

evidence.quote: To estimate the infall velocity we fitted the observed HCO$^{+}$ core spectrum with analytical infall models presented by (cite: Devries2005).

validation.value: None of the simple models reproduces the deep absorption

evidence.quote: We note that none of the simple models is able to reproduce the observed deep absorption feature (reaching zero intensity).

findings_qualitative.value: Fragmentation is inefficient: about 10 cores per clump versus about 160 Jeans masses

evidence.quote: showing that fragmentation is not efficient during the early stages of evolution

findings_qualitative.value: Protostellar-clump cores are warmer, with larger linewidths, than prestellar-clump cores

evidence.quote: Cores within the prestellar clump have smaller linewidths and lower temperatures than cores within the protostellar clump.

claims.experiment: HCO+ profiles and virial parameters of the cores
claims.result: Five of ten cores show inverse P Cygni profiles; five are sub-virial
claims.finding: Cores in the prestellar clump are undergoing collapse

evidence.quote: Half of these cores exhibit inverse P Cygni profiles in HCO$^{+}$ and are subvirialized indicating that they are undergoing collapse.

claims.hypothesis: The central protostellar-clump core is accreting from global collapse
claims.experiment: Hill5 fit to HCO+, Plummer profile fit, virial analysis
claims.result: Infall 1.6 km/s, infall rate 1.9e-2 Msun/yr, alpha_vir 0.71
claims.finding: Large-scale collapse feeds the massive core

evidence.quote: are consistent with a picture in which large-scale collapse is feeding gas into this core

claims.hypothesis: Core mass fraction increases with evolution
claims.experiment: Sum of core masses over clump mass
claims.finding: The protostellar clump has gathered more gas into cores, consistent with accretion

evidence.quote: The fraction of total mass in cores to clump mass is smaller in the prestellar clump ($\sim$6%) than in the protostellar clump ($\sim$23%).

claims.hypothesis: The CMF in early clump fragmentation is top-heavy
claims.experiment: MLE fit to the eCDF of 3 clumps
claims.finding: High-mass cores form more efficiently than low-mass cores

why_this_method.value: eCDF preferred over the differential CMF to avoid binning bias

evidence.quote: We prefer to use the eCDF over the differential form of the core mass function because the later approach contains the numerical bias introduced by binning.

limitations_admitted.value: Simple infall models fail to reproduce the deep HCO+ absorption

evidence.quote: To reproduce it requires a more sophisticated modeling, which is beyond the scope of this work.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only two clumps, so the evolutionary-sequence conclusion rests on a sample of two

CMF sample includes AGAL305 from different observations
